authors: Ryan LA, Hemmi JM, Collin SP, Hart NS
title: Electrophysiological measures of temporal resolution, contrast sensitivity and spatial resolving power in sharks
why: Measures flicker, contrast and acuity in the same sharks by one method, which would set the shark view's trails and blur together.

title: Ocular media transmission of coral reef fish: can coral reef fish see ultraviolet light?
why: Would show which reef families' lenses pass ultraviolet, deciding where the reef view's ultraviolet sheen belongs.

authors: Chung W-S, Marshall NJ, Watson S-A, Munday PL, Nilsson GE
title: Ocean acidification slows retinal function in a damselfish through interference with GABAA receptors
why: Holds the damselfish flicker value used by the earlier sheet (89 Hz), which would set the reef view's pace for a diurnal reef fish.

authors: McComb DM, Tricas TC, Kajiura SM
title: Enhanced visual fields in hammerhead sharks
why: The full text gives monocular and total visual fields of five sharks, replacing the shark view's invented field of 300 degrees.

title: Visual fields of four batoid fishes: a comparative study
why: The full text gives the vertical fields and blind areas of four rays, for placing the ray view's sharp band and dark underside.

authors: Foster TN, Williamson AG, Foster BR, Toomey MB
title: Light environment and seasonal variation in the visual system of the red shiner (Cyprinella lutrensis)
why: Would size the seasonal red shift proposed for minnows, now known from one 1982 shiner study.

title: Underwater refraction-polarization patterns of skylight perceived by aquatic animals through Snell's window of the flat water surface
why: Would give the geometry and appearance of Snell's window and the surface outside it as an aquatic animal sees them, for drawing the looking-up effect.

authors: Jinson ST, Liebich J, Senft SL, Mäthger LM
title: Retinal specializations and visual ecology in an animal with an extremely elaborate pupil shape: the little skate Leucoraja (Raja) erinacea
why: Would give the skate's pupil shape and how it shapes blur, for the ray view's pupil.

authors: Kalinoski M, Hirons A, Horodysky AZ, Brill RW
title: Spectral sensitivity, luminous sensitivity, and temporal resolution of the visual systems in three sympatric temperate coastal shark species
why: More shark flicker and dim-light values for the shark view's trails and shadows.

title: Teleost polarization vision: how it might work and what it might be good for
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
why: Review of how fish might read polarized light, for deciding whether any fish view should show it.

authors: Hawryshyn CW, Moyer HD, Allison WT, Haimberger TJ, McFarland WN
title: Multidimensional polarization sensitivity in damselfishes
why: Polarization sensitivity in adult damselfish, the largest reef family with measured eyes.

title: Peripheral hearing structures in fishes: diversity and sensitivity of catfishes and cichlids
journal: Advances in Experimental Medicine and Biology
why: Hearing ranges of catfish for the freshwater view's hearing row and microphone effect.

authors: Dreyfert T, Holmberg K, Struwe G
title: Critical flicker fusion frequency of the river lamprey (Lampetra fluviatilis)
why: A lamprey's flicker rate, for a later lamprey setting.

title: The eyes in three genera of hagfish (Eptatretus, Paramyxine and Myxine): a case of degenerative evolution
why: Confirms what hagfish eyes can detect, for the hagfish setting.

authors: Watt MJ, Evans CS, Joss JMP
title: Use of electroreception during foraging by the Australian lungfish
why: Electric sense in lungfish, which ride along with the freshwater view.
